name: Bellis perennis flower extract
description: Bellis perennis flower extract (CAS 84776-11-4 ), derived from the common daisy, is a botanical active sourced for its antioxidant and skin-conditioning properties in cosmetic formulations. Known commercially as daisy flower extract, it is sought by formulators targeting brightening and protective effects. In skincare, it is incorporated into serums, creams, and spot-treatment products targeting uneven skin tone and dullness. Its antioxidant activity supports formulation stability alongside skin benefit claims in finished personal care products. Color cosmetics manufacturers use it as a botanical ingredient in foundations and primers marketed with skin-care positioning. It also appears in hair care formulations, such as conditioners and scalp treatments, where its humectant properties support moisture retention. Nutraceutical and functional food developers have explored it as a botanical antioxidant additive, though cosmetic applications represent the primary commercial demand. The extract is valued for its versatility across multiple product categories. Bellis perennis flower extract is typically supplied as a liquid extract in water, glycerin, or glycol carrier systems. Dry powder forms are also available for encapsulated or anhydrous applications depending on the specific manufacturing needs. Standard supply grades include cosmetic-grade and natural or organic-certified variants aligned with international specifications. Concentration levels in commercial extracts vary by supplier, so buyers should confirm actives content against requirements. Formulators should verify carrier composition and quality standards to ensure compatibility with their existing production lines.
